# GitHub Copilot instructions

### AmbyKit usage

This project uses **AmbyKit** for Spec-Driven Development. Follow the workflow and rules in
`AGENTS.md`. The `/amby.*` prompts under `.github/prompts/` drive the phases.

<!-- ambykit:fingerprint 23808b22c31c -->
plain..github/prompts/amby.analyze.prompt.md:
---
description: "Cross-check spec, plan, and tasks for coverage, consistency, and dependency-graph health."
argument-hint: "[feature id, defaults to current]"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/analyze.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Analyze feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature) for consistency. Read-only — report, don't edit.

Check and report:

1. **Coverage:** every `FR-###`/`US-#` in the spec is addressed by the plan and has at least one
   task; every task maps to a real `US-#`. List orphans and gaps.
2. **Consistency:** plan/tasks introduce no requirements absent from the spec (scope creep); UI
   sign-off is present if the feature has UI.
3. **Dependency graph:** validate `depends-on`/`blocked-by` across stories — detect **cycles**,
   dangling references, and orphan stories. Report which stories are currently **blocked** vs
   **buildable now**.
4. **Clarity:** any remaining `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers.

Output a short, structured report (tables/bullets). Prefer machine-checkable facts over prose. Do not
modify any file.
plain..github/prompts/amby.clarify.prompt.md:
---
description: "Resolve the open [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers in a feature spec."
argument-hint: "[feature id, defaults to current]"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/clarify.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Resolve open questions in the spec for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

1. Read only that `spec.md`. Find every `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …]` marker.
2. For each, ask the user one concise, specific question. Offer a sensible default when one exists.
3. **Edit only the affected line(s)** — replace the marker with the resolved wording. Do not rewrite
   the rest of the file (token-frugal, non-destructive).
4. If an answer changes a requirement's testability, adjust just that `FR-###` or acceptance line.
5. When no markers remain, set the spec `status: ready` and report a one-line summary.

Do not add scope. If the user raises new scope, note it as a new `US-#` rather than expanding others.
plain..github/prompts/amby.constitution.prompt:
---
description: "Create or amend the project constitution — durable, cross-feature principles."
argument-hint: "[area to add or change, optional]"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/constitution.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Establish or update the project **constitution** at `.amby/constitution.md`.

1. If the file is missing, create it from `@.amby/templates/constitution.md` and fill it in. If it
   exists, amend only the section relevant to `${input:args}` (or, with no argument, review all principles briefly).
2. Interview the user only where a principle is unclear — ask one focused question at a time.
3. Keep each principle short, imperative, and **numbered** so later phases can cite it.
4. Cover: code quality, testing standards, UX consistency, performance/reliability, security. Add
   project-specific non-negotiables as needed.
5. Bump the version and update the date. Do not restate feature requirements — those belong in specs.

Output only the edited constitution. Be concise.
plain..github/prompts/amby.converge.prompt.md:
---
description: "Check the codebase against spec, plan, and tasks after implementing; append gap tasks, never edit code."
argument-hint: "[feature id, defaults to current]"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/converge.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Converge feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature): does the code satisfy its artifacts?
Never edit source code — only that feature's `tasks.md` and `spec.md` are writable.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot --phase=converge` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. No `tasks.md` → stop, say to run `/amby.tasks`. No `plan.md` → converge on spec + tasks and say so.
2. For every `FR-###`/`SC-###`, plan decision (incl. `data-model.md`/`contracts/`), and checked
   `T###`: look for evidence only in files the plan/tasks name. Classify **covered**, **gap**
   (absent), or **unverified** (inconclusive). Skip items the plan marks deferred/out of scope.
3. **Append, don't rewrite.** Under `## Convergence` in `tasks.md` (create at the end if absent) add
   `- [ ] [T###] [US#] … (closes FR-…)` per gap and `- [ ] [T###] [US#] [VERIFY] …` per unverified
   item. Continue IDs from the highest `T###` anywhere in the file; skip items already listed
   unchecked there. Nothing to add → leave the file untouched.
4. In `spec.md`, patch only `status:` lines: a story → `done` when every FR/SC it maps to is
   covered; the feature → `done` when all stories are.
5. Report: **converged** (no gaps) or **gaps found (N)**, counts per class, and a table of every ID
   with its class and a one-line reason for each gap/unverified item.
plain..github/prompts/amby.design.prompt.md:
---
description: "Design the UI — wireframes, component specs, and design tokens — with a sign-off gate."
argument-hint: "[feature id, defaults to current]"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/design.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Design the UI for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read that feature's `spec.md`, the templates `@.amby/templates/ui.md` +
`@.amby/templates/design-tokens.json`, and — for detailed rules — `@.amby/reference/design-conventions.md`.
Design for the spec's user stories.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot --phase=design` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. Write `ui.md` following the template: per story, a layout/wireframe (ASCII or embedded SVG), a
   component inventory (props + full state set + token names), interaction criteria in
   Given/When/Then tied to the `US-#`, and content/accessibility notes (WCAG AA).
2. Write/extend `design-tokens.json` in three tiers — primitive → semantic → component. In `ui.md`
   cite semantic/component token **names**, never raw values.
3. Keep the UI consistent with any constitution UX principle (cite by number).
4. **Sign-off gate:** present the design and ask the user to approve. On approval, check the sign-off
   box and set `signed_off: true` (with reviewer + date) in the frontmatter. Until then it's a draft.

Downstream phases treat a signed-off UI as binding.
plain..github/prompts/amby.implement.prompt.md:
---
description: "Execute the task list, checking off tasks and updating story status as you go."
argument-hint: "[task id or story id, defaults to next unblocked]"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/implement.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Implement work for `${input:args}` (default: the next unblocked task in priority order).

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot --phase=implement` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. From `tasks.md`, pick the target task(s). Respect the Foundational-before-features gate and the
   story dependency graph — never start a task whose story is `blocked-by` unfinished work.
2. Load **only** the slice you need: the task line, the relevant `plan.md` section, and the specific
   files named. Don't read the whole spec tree (token-frugal).
3. Implement to satisfy the mapped `FR-###`/acceptance criteria and the constitution. Add/adjust
   tests for the acceptance criteria.
4. **Patch in place:** flip the completed task's checkbox to `- [x]` in `tasks.md`; when all of a
   story's tasks are done, set that story's `status: done` in `spec.md` (or `in-progress` while
   partway). Don't rewrite untouched sections. After each checked task, run
   `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot --phase=implement --task=T###` (ignore errors).
5. Report what you did and the next unblocked task. Stop at a story checkpoint for review.
plain..github/prompts/amby.plan.prompt.md:
---
description: "Produce the technical implementation plan (the HOW) from an approved spec and UI."
argument-hint: "[feature id, defaults to current]"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/plan.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Write the implementation plan for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read that feature's `spec.md` and `ui.md`, plus `@.amby/constitution.md`.

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot --phase=plan` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. Write `plan.md` following `@.amby/templates/plan.md`: technical context (stack, libraries,
   constraints), architecture, and a phased approach (Phase 0 research → Phase 1 foundation → feature phases).
2. This is the **first artifact with technology decisions.** Ensure every choice honors the
   constitution (cite principle numbers).
3. Map each `FR-###`/`US-#` to how the design satisfies it. **Reference by ID — do not restate the
   spec.** Flag any requirement you can't satisfy as a risk.
4. Generate supporting artifacts only if needed: `data-model.md` (entities/invariants),
   `contracts/` (API/interface specs), `research.md` (decisions with rationale).
5. Do not invent requirements not in the spec; if you find a gap, note it and suggest a `clarify`.

Keep the plan lean; link to spec/UI rather than duplicating.
plain..github/prompts/amby.review.prompt.md:
---
description: "Review an artifact from another role's perspective — findings by stable ID, advisory only."
argument-hint: "<artifact path> [--as <role id>] [--apply]"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/review.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Review `${input:args}` (an artifact path, e.g. `specs/NNN-slug/spec.md`) as a **different** role.
If the path does not exist, stop and name the phase that produces it.

1. Pick the reviewer: `--as <id>` → `@.amby/roles/<id>.md`; otherwise QA for a spec or tasks,
   Architect for a plan, PM for a UI design. If the file is missing, stop and list `.amby/roles/`.
   Say which role you are acting as in your first line.
2. Read only the artifact (and its spec, if reviewing a plan or tasks). Apply the role's focus
   checklist. Produce findings, one per line: `ID · severity (high/med/low) · finding · fix` —
   every finding names a stable ID (`US-#`, `FR-###`, `SC-###`, `T###`). Modify nothing.
3. Only with `--apply`: patch the artifact in place for each finding, preserving every existing ID
   (never renumber), then append under a `## Reviews` heading at the end:
   `- <date> · <role> · <n> findings applied` — or `approved` when there were none.
4. This is advisory: no phase waits on a review. End with the findings count and the next phase to run.
plain..github/prompts/amby.revise.prompt.md:
---
description: "Continue an existing feature's spec (or design) — add and refine in place, with a done-guard."
argument-hint: "[feature id, defaults to current] + what to add or refine"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/revise.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Continue the spec (and, optionally, the design) for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read only that feature's `spec.md` (and its `ui.md` if continuing design) plus the structure
of `@.amby/templates/spec.md`. This command **extends** an existing feature — it is not `specify`
(which starts a new feature) nor `clarify` (which only resolves `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers).

1. Resolve the feature dir `specs/NNN-slug/`. If it — or its `spec.md` — cannot be found, report a
   clear error and make **no** changes.
2. **Done-guard.** If the `spec.md` frontmatter `status:` is `done`, make no edits: tell the author the
   feature is complete and to run `/amby.specify` for a new feature. Stop here.
3. Otherwise **continue in place** (patch, never regenerate — Principle 3):
   - Add new user stories (`US-#`), requirements (`FR-###`), and success criteria (`SC-###`), each
     taking the **next available number**. Preserve every existing id and its text verbatim.
   - Refine existing items only where the author asked; keep their ids stable.
   - New requirements use EARS (SHALL / WHEN / WHILE / IF-THEN / WHERE); new acceptance criteria use
     Given/When/Then — consistent with `specify`.
   - Leave any story already marked `status: done` untouched; you may still add new stories.
4. Set the `spec.md` frontmatter `status:` to `in-progress`.
5. **Design (optional).** If the author is continuing the UI/design and `ui.md` exists, extend it in
   place, preserving existing sections. If `ui.md` does **not** exist, do not create it here — direct
   the author to run `/amby.design`.
6. Keep edits minimal and token-frugal; cite the constitution by principle number where relevant.

Report what you added or changed, by id.
plain..github/prompts/amby.specify.prompt.md:
---
description: "Turn a feature idea into a spec — user stories, EARS requirements, acceptance criteria."
argument-hint: "<feature description>"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/specify.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Write a specification for: **${input:args}**

Context: read `@.amby/constitution.md` and the structure of `@.amby/templates/spec.md` only. Do not
read other specs.

1. Create the feature dir `specs/NNN-slug/` (next number, kebab-slug from the title) and write
   `spec.md` following `@.amby/templates/spec.md`. Then run
   `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot --phase=specify` with the new number; ignore any error.
2. Define **user stories** (`US-#`): role / capability / benefit, a priority (P1/P2/P3), why that
   priority, an independent-test statement, and `depends-on`/`blocked-by` if any. Set `status: draft`.
3. Write **acceptance criteria** in Given/When/Then per story.
4. Write **functional requirements** (`FR-###`) in EARS notation (SHALL / WHEN / WHILE / IF-THEN /
   WHERE). Each must be testable.
5. Write measurable, tech-agnostic **success criteria** (`SC-###`).
6. **Capture WHAT/WHY only — no technology choices.** Flag every unknown inline as
   `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …]` instead of guessing.
7. If `.amby/config.json` has `"worktrees": true` and this is a git repo, run
   `ambykit worktree NNN-slug` (the only command to run) and tell the user to continue in
   `.worktrees/NNN-slug/`. Otherwise skip this step (say why if isolation was enabled but git is absent).

Keep it tight. Reference the constitution by principle number where relevant; don't restate it.
plain..github/prompts/amby.tasks.prompt.md:
---
description: "Break the plan into an ordered, dependency-aware task checklist."
argument-hint: "[feature id, defaults to current]"
agent: agent
---
<!-- GENERATED by AmbyKit from src/prompts/tasks.md — do not edit by hand; run `ambykit sync`. -->

Generate `tasks.md` for feature `${input:args}` (default: the current feature).

Context: read that feature's `plan.md` (and `spec.md` for story IDs/priorities/dependencies).

Run `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot --phase=tasks` first, with that feature's number; ignore any error.

1. Write tasks following `@.amby/templates/tasks.md` as checkbox lines:
   `- [ ] [T###] [P?] [US#] description (file/path)`.
2. Group into phases: **Setup → Foundational → User stories (by priority) → Polish**. Enforce the
   gate: no user-story task before Foundational completes.
3. Order tasks by the story **dependency graph** (`depends-on`/`blocked-by`) and priority. Mark
   independent tasks `[P]`. Tag each task with its `[US#]`. End each story group with a checkpoint.
4. Give every task a stable `T###` id and a concrete file path.

Do not start implementing. Keep descriptions to one line each.
plain.AGENTS.md:
# AGENTS.md — demo

### AmbyKit usage

This project uses **AmbyKit** for Spec-Driven Development. Build features by producing structured
artifacts before code: a constitution, specs (user stories + EARS requirements), UI design, a plan,
and an ordered task list.

**Workflow commands**

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/amby.constitution` | Create or amend the project constitution — durable, cross-feature principles. |
| `/amby.specify` | Turn a feature idea into a spec — user stories, EARS requirements, acceptance criteria. |
| `/amby.clarify` | Resolve the open [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers in a feature spec. |
| `/amby.revise` | Continue an existing feature's spec (or design) — add and refine in place, with a done-guard. |
| `/amby.design` | Design the UI — wireframes, component specs, and design tokens — with a sign-off gate. |
| `/amby.plan` | Produce the technical implementation plan (the HOW) from an approved spec and UI. |
| `/amby.tasks` | Break the plan into an ordered, dependency-aware task checklist. |
| `/amby.analyze` | Cross-check spec, plan, and tasks for coverage, consistency, and dependency-graph health. |
| `/amby.implement` | Execute the task list, checking off tasks and updating story status as you go. |
| `/amby.converge` | Check the codebase against spec, plan, and tasks after implementing; append gap tasks, never edit code. |
| `/amby.review` | Review an artifact from another role's perspective — findings by stable ID, advisory only. |

**Rules for agents**

- Read `.amby/constitution.md` and honor its principles in every phase.
- Specs (`specs/NNN-*/spec.md`) capture WHAT/WHY with **no technology choices**; plans capture HOW.
- Requirements use EARS (WHEN/WHILE/IF…THE SYSTEM SHALL…) with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.
- Reference artifacts by stable id (US-#, FR-###, SC-###); don't restate them. Patch in place.
- Task checkboxes in `tasks.md` are the source of truth for progress (`ambykit dashboard`).
- **Current feature** (when a phase gets no id): the enclosing `.worktrees/NNN-slug/` directory if
  the project root is one; else the git branch, if it names a `specs/` dir; else the highest-numbered
  `specs/` dir — say which you chose. `ambykit worktree <id>` gives a feature its own working copy.

<!-- ambykit:fingerprint 56b894b1d65a -->

   story dependency graph — never start a task whose story is `blocked-by` unfinished work.
2. Load **only** the slice you need: the task line, the relevant `plan.md` section, and the specific
   files named. Don't read the whole spec tree (token-frugal).
3. Implement to satisfy the mapped `FR-###`/acceptance criteria and the constitution. Add/adjust
   tests for the acceptance criteria.
4. **Patch in place:** flip the completed task's checkbox to `- [x]` in `tasks.md`; when all of a
   story's tasks are done, set that story's `status: done` in `spec.md` (or `in-progress` while
   partway). Don't rewrite untouched sections. After each checked task, run
   `ambykit activity <feature> --agent=copilot --phase=implement --task=T###` (ignore errors).
5. Report what you did and the next unblocked task. Stop at a story checkpoint for review.

   `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: …]` instead of guessing.

   `ambykit worktree NNN-slug` (the only command to run) and tell the user to continue in

roles.AGENTS.md:
# AGENTS.md — demo

### AmbyKit usage

This project uses **AmbyKit** for Spec-Driven Development. Build features by producing structured
artifacts before code: a constitution, specs (user stories + EARS requirements), UI design, a plan,
and an ordered task list.

**Workflow commands**

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/amby.constitution` | Create or amend the project constitution — durable, cross-feature principles. |
| `/amby.specify` | Turn a feature idea into a spec — user stories, EARS requirements, acceptance criteria. |
| `/amby.clarify` | Resolve the open [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers in a feature spec. |
| `/amby.revise` | Continue an existing feature's spec (or design) — add and refine in place, with a done-guard. |
| `/amby.design` | Design the UI — wireframes, component specs, and design tokens — with a sign-off gate. |
| `/amby.plan` | Produce the technical implementation plan (the HOW) from an approved spec and UI. |
| `/amby.tasks` | Break the plan into an ordered, dependency-aware task checklist. |
| `/amby.analyze` | Cross-check spec, plan, and tasks for coverage, consistency, and dependency-graph health. |
| `/amby.implement` | Execute the task list, checking off tasks and updating story status as you go. |
| `/amby.converge` | Check the codebase against spec, plan, and tasks after implementing; append gap tasks, never edit code. |
| `/amby.review` | Review an artifact from another role's perspective — findings by stable ID, advisory only. |

**Rules for agents**

- Read `.amby/constitution.md` and honor its principles in every phase.
- Specs (`specs/NNN-*/spec.md`) capture WHAT/WHY with **no technology choices**; plans capture HOW.
- Requirements use EARS (WHEN/WHILE/IF…THE SYSTEM SHALL…) with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.
- Reference artifacts by stable id (US-#, FR-###, SC-###); don't restate them. Patch in place.
- Task checkboxes in `tasks.md` are the source of truth for progress (`ambykit dashboard`).
- **Current feature** (when a phase gets no id): the enclosing `.worktrees/NNN-slug/` directory if
  the project root is one; else the git branch, if it names a `specs/` dir; else the highest-numbered
  `specs/` dir — say which you chose. `ambykit worktree <id>` gives a feature its own working copy.
